value: The results showed an interaction of perspective and valence in both the right and left amygdala. In the right hemisphere, amygdala activation was lower when viewing negative images from the perspective of the tough vs. the sensitive target; in the left hemisphere, amygdala activation was marginally lower for the tough vs. sensitive perspective. There was no significant difference for neutral images.

description.value: fMRI preprocessing using SPM8, including slice-timing correction, realignment, spatial normalization, interpolation, and smoothing.

spans.text: Imaging data were preprocessed using SPM8 (Wellcome Department of Cognitive Neurology).

A slice-timing correction to the first slice was performed followed by realignment of the images to the first image. Next, data were spatially normalized to an EPI template based on the MNI305 stereotactic space. Normalized images were interpolated to 2-mm 3 voxels and smoothed with a 6-mm full-width-at-half-maximum (FWHM) Gaussian kernel.

Significant clusters were identified using joint voxel and extent thresholds that preserved an α of less than 0.05, as determined by AlphaSim (1,000 iterations; smoothness estimated at 11.5 mm from the residual of the corresponding second-level regression), implemented in NeuroElf (uncorrected P < 0.02 and 253 contiguous voxels).
